## Description {#details}

These functions are responsible for initialising the test runner and returning the test result as the process exit code. Proper initialisation ensures that the µTest++ framework is correctly configured to manage and execute test cases, while the exit code reflects the overall outcome of the tests, supporting integration with automated build and continuous integration systems.

The simplest test consists of a single test case containing a single expectation; for example:


<ProgramListing extension="cpp">

<CodeLine><Highlight kind="preprocessor">#include &lt;<Link to="/docs/api/files/include/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus-h">micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus.h</Link>&gt;</Highlight><Highlight kind="normal"></Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal"></Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal"></Highlight><Highlight kind="keywordtype">int</Highlight><Highlight kind="normal"></Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">main(</Highlight><Highlight kind="keywordtype">int</Highlight><Highlight kind="normal"> argc, </Highlight><Highlight kind="keywordtype">char</Highlight><Highlight kind="normal">&#42; argv[])</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">&#123;</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">  </Highlight><Highlight kind="keyword">namespace </Highlight><Highlight kind="normal">mt = <Link to="/docs/api/namespaces/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus">micro&#95;os&#95;plus::micro&#95;test&#95;plus</Link>;</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal"></Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">  mt::initialize(argc, argv, </Highlight><Highlight kind="stringliteral">&quot;Minimal&quot;</Highlight><Highlight kind="normal">);</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal"></Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">  mt::test&#95;case (</Highlight><Highlight kind="stringliteral">&quot;Check truth&quot;</Highlight><Highlight kind="normal">, [] &#123;</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">    mt::expect (</Highlight><Highlight kind="keyword">true</Highlight><Highlight kind="normal">);</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">  &#125;)</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal"></Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">  </Highlight><Highlight kind="keywordflow">return</Highlight><Highlight kind="normal"> mt::exit&#95;code ();</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">&#125;</Highlight></CodeLine>

</ProgramListing>

When this test is executed, the output is as follows:


<ProgramListing extension="console">

<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">• Minimal - test suite started</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">  ✓ Check truth - test case passed (1 check)</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">✓ Minimal - test suite passed (1 check in 1 test case)</Highlight></CodeLine>

</ProgramListing>

### exit&#95;code() {#gaa790667969dc1a261c324e89a6ea4591}

<MemberDefinition
  prototype={<>int micro&#95;os&#95;plus::micro&#95;test&#95;plus::exit&#95;code (void)</>}
  labels = {["nodiscard"]}>
Complete the test run and return the exit code.

<SectionUser title="Parameters">
None.
</SectionUser>


<SectionUser title="Returns">
0 if all tests were successful, 1 if any test failed.
</SectionUser>

In addition to the test cases defined in <code>main()</code>, additional test suites may be declared as static objects either within the same file or in other files, and are automatically registered via the static constructors mechanism.

The <code>exit&#95;code</code> function finalises the execution of all registered test suites and test cases within the µTest++ framework, and returns an appropriate exit code to the operating system. This function should be called at the end of the test program, typically from the <code>main()</code> function, to ensure that all results are properly reported and the correct status is communicated.

The returned value indicates the overall success or failure of the test run, allowing integration with build systems and continuous integration environments.

### initialize() {#gac2c60d60578f668878957ec68a37538f}

<MemberDefinition
  prototype={<>void micro&#95;os&#95;plus::micro&#95;test&#95;plus::initialize (int argc, char &#42; argv=[], const char &#42; name=&quot;Main&quot;)</>}>
Initialise the µTest++ framework.

<ParametersList title="Parameters">
<ParametersListItem name="[in] argc">The number of command-line arguments.</ParametersListItem>
<ParametersListItem name="[in] argv">Array of pointers to null-terminated argument strings.</ParametersListItem>
<ParametersListItem name="[in] name">The name of the default test suite. Defaults to <code>&quot;Main&quot;</code> if not specified.</ParametersListItem>
</ParametersList>

<SectionUser title="Returns">
Nothing.
</SectionUser>

The <code>initialize</code> function sets up the µTest++ testing framework, preparing it for test execution. It processes command-line arguments, configures the test environment, and establishes the default test suite name. This function should be called at the beginning of the test programme, typically from the <code>main()</code> function, to ensure proper initialisation of all framework components.

The provided arguments may be used to configure verbosity or other run-time options for the test session.
